title: MAM-Care – Maternal involvement, centeredness, safety and care in obstetrics - a multidimensional analysis (interventional study)
summary:
The MAM-Care study is funded by the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology, and Space and investigates satisfaction with obstetric care from the perspectives of mothers and care providers. The focus is on woman-centeredness and maternal autonomy during childbirth, which are key determinants of maternal satisfaction. In addition, the study addresses safety and quality of care during the birth process in accordance with the S3 guideline “Vaginal Birth at Term.”

In the first phase of the study, the current state of obstetric care in Germany was assessed. To this end, all maternity departments nationwide were contacted, and in cooperation with two statutory health insurance providers, 4,000 mothers were invited to participate in a written survey. In the survey, 98% of physicians and 99% of midwives reported that women in labor should be encouraged to change positions. In contrast, 43% of mothers who had experienced a vaginal birth stated that they had not been encouraged to do so. The most frequently reported final birth position was the supine position (57.7%). Moreover, 32% of mothers indicated that they were not able to freely choose their final birth position. Further analysis revealed that maternal satisfaction was not determined by the specific birth position itself, but rather by whether it was chosen autonomously or externally determined. 

Against this background, in the second part of the study (starting in May 2025), a low-threshold intervention will be implemented and evaluated in six obstetric hospitals. The aim is to empower and encourage women in labor and their companions to try out different positions during childbirth. The intervention seeks to strengthen women’s ability to recognize their own preferences regarding birth positions during labor and to communicate these to care providers. This will be supported through movement-promoting information materials and visual aids, among others.
conditions: Single delivery by forceps and vacuum extractor

Birth companions after birth: n=600 (control phase), n=600 (intervention phase)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Mothers: Vaginal live birth in one of the participating obstetrics departments
Birth companions: Accompanying a mother in the delivery room from the study population
Documentation: Full survey of all live births
Midwives: Midwives employed at the participating departments
Physicians: Physicians employed at the participating departments
Exclusion criteria:
For the maternal survey and the birth companions: Cesarean section birth
